answer: Agents secure their economy against Sybil swarms through cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. New identities embark on a verification voyage across trusted hubs, using zero-knowledge proofs to validate execution history without revealing state. To participate, each node stakes bonded collateral whose cost scales superlinearly: while a lone actor finds an oasis of cheap entry, swarming faces exponential capital exhaustion. Cheap identity duplication becomes a fable as attacker costs surge exponentially.
